tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>

===================== 01-member-context-updates.md
# 01 — 连续工作不重复背景，压缩后恢复当前信息

**What to build:** Member 初次工作或背景缺失时得到完整起步信息；工作中只收到对应类别的变化，memory 更新不重发全文，责任或 Workspace 撤销仍明确呈现。实现完整流程 F1，不改变普通 Session。
**Blocked by:** None — can start immediately
**Status:** complete

验证：真实 Session 分类注入/投影/恢复测试与 Host/tools 回归通过；固定 synthetic 场景已重跑，详见实施记录。

- [x] 连续多步使用真实累积的 Session surface；无变化不追加，memory 修改后只追加一次提示，后续不退化为每步重发。
- [x] identity、ownership、Workspace 分别更新；完整当前列表替代对应旧列表，覆盖撤销为空和多 Workspace 缩为一个。
- [x] ownership/Workspace 变化不重发 memory，memory 更新不重发其它类别；不保留第二套注入策略或开关。
- [x] memory 的完整基线与后续更新提示分别识别；压缩后仅剩提示时补最新完整基线，而不是误认为背景齐全。
- [x] 索引删除、不可读、超预算均说明当前异常和入口；保留现有预算与记忆权限，不要求每次自己写完再读取。
- [x] 删除动态块中不必要的稳定教学，保留使用路径等基本事实；本票只调整自身文案，不提前大改全局 persona。
- [x] 更新 member-memory/context 和 Host authority 的正式双语说明及相关 README、CHANGELOG；不把未落地的其它票写成现行行为。
- [x] 同一固定场景比较注入次数、重复正文与当前 surface 占用；不沿用历史 80% 指标作为成功门槛。跑窄的注入与恢复测试，覆盖 F1。

===================== 02-thread-rejection-recovery.md
# 02 — Thread 写入被拒后，根据完整变化重新提交

**What to build:** 普通长度 Thread 消息导致写入被拒时，拒绝结果完整提供变化和真实可用的恢复路径；Agent 可修改行动再提交，不必重复读取同一正文。实现 F4 的 Thread Message 路径，同时移除旧的正文模糊匹配。
**Blocked by:** None — can start immediately
**Status:** complete

验证：Host/tools 1081 passed、1 原有 skipped；补充部分拒绝→read→提交后相关 24 tests 通过。真实模型 F4 留在 07，付费调用仍未获授权。

- [x] 通过真实工具执行→Session 工具结果→下一次 Host 写入路径测试，不用永远返回 true 的可见性 fake 代替整个验收。
- [x] 从当前 surface 派生 Team 来源、具体事实身份及实际完整文本；通知和工具结果都可提供 Thread Message；不建立独立已读事实库。
- [x] 裁剪后保留的 metadata 不单独证明完整，摘要、预览、模型复述、相同短正文或另一 Thread 的同文均不误命中。
- [x] unread_required 与 stale_revision 的结果和恢复句一致：完整补齐则允许重新考虑，缺少必要事实则给读取入口；不承诺重试一定提交，不把不匹配凭据说成单纯并发变化。
- [x] 拒绝本身不写 Thread 已读、不消费 marker；后续写入仍校验新到事实、revision、权限和 Task 状态。
- [x] 只覆盖可完整提供的消息路径；大批或超长拒绝明确说明未提供全部并要求读取，续读由后续票完成，绝不因本票省调用而放行不完整内容。
- [x] 更新所有受本票影响的工具文档、boundary 文档、package README、persona/core skill 恢复规则及测试；其它未完成路径如 Main/Activity 仍按实际行为陈述。
- [x] 跑 Thread 真实 ledger/Session 组合与 tool render 测试；完整→重考虑→成功、部分→读取、新事实→再次拒绝均有可核对输出。模型 F4 在最终组合评测中验证。

===================== 03-read-and-reentry.md
# 03 — read 恢复讨论并确认已读，不重复已提供正文

**What to build:** 普通长度 Thread/Main read 根据当前上下文补必要背景、提供时间顺序的未读批次并确认对应内容；已完整可见的正文可以省略。无未读时仍能恢复讨论，覆盖 F2、F5 和 F3 的确认阶段。
**Blocked by:** 02
**Status:** complete

Thread 部分已于 `241f8f8` 提交；Main 的查询/直接通知正文省略、压缩后背景恢复与再次read已通过真实 Session 测试。读取与确认在队列内选择，Main 不会因后续 Task 卡遮住更早未读。详见实施记录。

- [x] 没有“继续/重入”模式参数：当前上下文有背景则以新增为主，缺少背景或无未读主动查看时补主题、少量最近原文、必要回复对象和当前 Task/Claim 状态。
- [x] 不用永久“曾读过”标记判断背景是否还在；不增加模型摘要调用；原文不足时明确继续读 history/message。
- [x] read 对已完整可见的事实说明本次确认及正文省略；新到或已不可完整见的事实正常提供，无每次回复后强制调用规则。
- [x] 背景、未读、当前状态、Thread card 分开表示；history/message、自动背景和通知不主动确认，不改变 Attention。
- [x] Host 的批次选择与确认范围一致，不在 read 已确认后由 renderer 删除必要正文；Human Remote 原有读取行为不因 Agent 背景策略改变。
- [x] 使用真实累计 Session 验证再次 read 不持续重复背景；压缩后无未读可以恢复，且无已读变化时不新增读 operation。
- [x] 保留历史 ledger receipt 的可重放性；如新增 Agent 读取选择，持久确认范围可由记录确定，不依赖 replay 时的 Session。不得直接修改旧固定批次解释。
- [x] 首次 read→查看分工→claim 与压缩后 read→继续工作均有端到端证据；更新相关双语读取、上下文和 Host 文档及 CHANGELOG。触及 Remote/assembled Web 时执行 browser 检查。

===================== 04-long-message-continuation.md
# 04 — 长消息能续读，完整提供前不确认

**What to build:** Thread/Main 的长消息通过现有 team_thread read/message 连续读取；输出有界、每步能前进，完整交付后按 read 或查询的性质处理确认。实现 F6，不增加第八个工具。
**Blocked by:** 03
**Status:** complete

Thread/Main read 与 message 复用同一缺段续读规则；真实 Session 覆盖中文/emoji逐字拼接、中段丢失、单独末段、无未读长背景、查询后read省略确认、后续消息不跨过未完整消息、容量拒绝。Session restore 与新旧 ledger receipt replay 分别验证；没有付费模型评测。

- [x] 普通消息仍尽量全文；批次先减少条数，单条确实放不下才分段。预算包含外层文字、状态及续读入口。
- [x] 用一个系统提供的续读方式推进不可变消息，明确消息身份、当前片段、是否结束；不让模型选择多套 offset/limit 协议。
- [x] read 续读完整后确认对应事实；message 续读不确认，后续 read 可确认且不重复正文。未完整的消息不能被跨过而推进连续已读水位。
- [x] 新接口在选择批次时确定确认范围；当前 Session 的片段可见性不成为 ledger replay 依赖，旧读记录重放不变。
- [x] 精确覆盖整段正文，不因多字节字符或分割边界丢字；截断通知、末段单独存在、当前 surface 缺段均不能冒充完整。
- [x] 正常连续读取有进展，中断后可以继续；裁剪/压缩缺段时明确补读，不反复返同一开头或错误确认。实际超出模型可承载容量时明确限制，不假装已读完。
- [x] 对消息附件只给读取入口，不把消息全文等同附件全文；不新增通用大文件系统或备用无限输出路径。
- [x] F6 真实工具/Session/Host 流程通过，含没有未读的 message 查询、长消息后跟新消息、Thread/Main、重启重放。更新类型、tool 说明、双语正式文档和 CHANGELOG；按 Remote 影响执行相应检查。

===================== 05-main-and-activity-recovery.md
# 05 — Main 与 Task 变化采用一致的阅读恢复规则

**What to build:** Main 完整直接通知可支持正常 post；Task/Claim 事件完整提供后可支持对应操作重新判断，和 Thread Message 使用同一阅读原则。实现 F3 和 F4 的其它事实类型，不统一本来不同的权限与凭据。
**Blocked by:** 02、04
**Status:** complete

- [x] Main 通知完整提供全部必要事实后可 post，无需重复正文；Main 不新增 Thread revision 凭据；新的必要未读仍拦截。
- [x] Activity 按实际事件定义必要字段，完整提供操作者、对象及变化；看板当前状态、Thread card 和摘要不等同完整事件。
- [x] 通知、read/history/message、拒绝结果的同一事实使用一致判断；不依据来自哪种出口区别放行。
- [x] 阅读条件满足不写水位或消费 marker；显式 read 才确认，完整可见内容不重复；权限、Task 关闭、验收人资格仍由既有 Host 检查。
- [x] Main/Activity 长内容或多条变化未完整时走 04 的读取入口，不遗留另一种无限拒绝正文路径。
- [x] F3 通知→post→read 验证三种状态彼此独立；Task 变化→拒绝→重新判断覆盖 Message 与 Activity 混合未读及新变化到达。
- [x] 一次清理受影响的旧 recovery 句、凭据说法和专门绕过路径；更新正式双语工具、boundary、Attention/messaging 文档及相关 README/CHANGELOG。
- [x] 跑真实 Main/Activity ledger/Session 与 tool 测试；根据 Host/Remote 接口影响执行类型及 browser 检查，不以 render snapshot 单独验收。

# 06 — 通知优先展示直接信号，不重复无用正文

**What to build:** Agent 在有界通知中先看到直接提及和责任变化，普通更新仍只有计数和入口；省略有明确说明，阅读指引与实际缺失一致，不改既有投递与未读语义。

- [x] 普通 Thread/Main 更新只给数量和入口，DM 不进入 Inbox 或虚构 Thread；已知正文不反复挤占新信号。
- [x] 通知上限含包装、计数和入口；直接信号优先于普通计数，省略重要内容明确“仍有直接通知未展开”，可从 Inbox/Thread 读取。
- [x] 通知全文/截断声明和 05 的可见性判断一致；完整提供后不机械要求先 read，部分提供时给可执行入口。
- [x] 真实通知投递前后直接断言未读数量和 markers 不变，不能只检查日志“未读”文字；显式 read 后才改变。

**Blocked by:** None — can start immediately
**Status:** complete

验证：Host/tools 1081 passed、1 原有 skipped；补充部分拒绝→read→提交后相关 24 tests 通过。真实模型 F4 留在 07，付费调用仍未获授权。

- [x] 通过真实工具执行→Session 工具结果→下一次 Host 写入路径测试，不用永远返回 true 的可见性 fake 代替整个验收。

1	# Agent 工具与上下文呈现：已确认设计
2	
3	**确认日期：2026-10-29。** Human 已确认目标、具体行为和六段完整流程；本稿将讨论整理为实施依据。同日另行授权推进实施；进度见 README。本稿不描述当前产品行为，现行行为仍以源码、测试和正式文档为准。
4	
5	## 1. 目标与范围
6	
7	首要目标是 Agent 正确理解当前状态并完成协作；其次是减少重复上下文、重复读取和无效重试。不以整体压缩比例驱动改造，不因文字缩短就判定成功。
8	
9	范围覆盖七个 Team 工具、Agent 通知、Member 动态 context、persona 与 core skills。有证据的行为问题可以修正，但行为变化与文案整理分别验证。保留七个工具的职责、权限、Attention 和 Task/Claim 语义；不改 Human Web Client 交互、不改 Harness 仓库、agent loop 或 shipped defaults。
10	
11	工程细节由实施者决定：优先复用现有能力，选能够长期保留的最简单实现，不为假设需求引入通用框架、配置开关、备用实现或独立事实数据库。
12	
13	## 2. 三个不同的状态
14	
15	| 状态 | 含义 | 不意味着什么 |
16	| --- | --- | --- |
17	| 当前上下文已提供某事实 | 来源和对象明确，必要内容完整出现在本次模型可用的上下文中 | 不等于模型理解正确，不等于持久已读 |
18	| 已确认已读 | 显式 `read` 确认的事实，由 Host 写入既有阅读状态 | 不等于事项完成，不改变 Attention |
19	| 操作已提交 | Host 按当前权限、状态及并发条件提交操作 | 不等于通知送达，不顺带清除未读 |
20	
21	收到通知、发回复、`history`、`message` 查询和自动背景补充都不主动确认已读。`read` 可以省略当前上下文里已经完整提供的正文，但必须明确确认了哪些内容、哪些正文被省略、还有多少未读。
22	
23	历史已读不会因压缩而撤销；压缩可能导致 Agent 缺少工作背景，需要重新提供。当前上下文中的完整性只是本次阅读条件的依据，不建立第二套持久未读状态。
24	
25	## 3. Member 背景与记忆
26	
27	- 新会话或上下文缺少起步背景时，提供当前身份、Project ownership、Workspace 参与及路径、预算内完整 memory 索引。
28	- 没有变化时不追加重复内容。
29	- 自己修改 `memory.md` 后，只提供简短更新提示，明确先前副本不再代表最新文件；不强迫立即读取刚写过的文件。
30	- 身份、ownership、Workspace 分别更新；ownership 和 Workspace 变化提供各自完整当前列表，包含撤销为空或从多个参与缩为一个的情况。
31	- 不因责任变化重发 memory，不因 memory 更新重发身份和 Workspace。
32	- memory 删除、不可读或超过既有预算时，明确异常及读取/维护入口，不继续把旧副本当成当前索引。
33	- 压缩后按当前实际缺失的类别补足背景；不能因为还残留一条 memory 更新提示，就假定完整索引仍在。
34	- 记忆是可能过时的参考，不覆盖 Human 输入、Workspace 指令和 Team durable facts。
35	
36	## 4. 读取与恢复讨论
37	
38	`read` 负责分批提供未读、显式确认已读，并补足必要的讨论背景；不新增由模型选择的“继续/重新进入”模式。
39	
40	- 连续讨论：新增事实全文为主，附必要回复对象和当前 Task/Claim 状态，不重复大片历史。
41	- 首次进入、压缩后背景缺失、无未读但主动查看：提供讨论主题、少量最近原文、必要引用对象和当前状态。
42	- 背景判断使用当前上下文，不用永久的“以前读过”标记。无法可靠判断时补少量背景，不默认模型记得。
43	- 背景选取使用原文和既有结构化状态；不额外调用模型生成摘要。
44	- 背景、当前状态、未读事实明确区分。背景不主动推进阅读状态，也不把 Thread card 当成已读完其 Thread。
45	- 当前批次的正文及必要回复对象优先于额外背景。未提供的历史和附件给出入口；完整消息不代表附件已读。
46	- 未读按时间顺序分批，不为了展示最新结论跳过旧的必要事实。

**确认日期：2026-10-29。** Human 已确认目标、具体行为和六段完整流程；本稿将讨论整理为实施依据。同日另行授权推进实施；进度见 README。本稿不描述当前产品行为，现行行为仍以源码、测试和正式文档为准。

## 1. 目标与范围

首要目标是 Agent 正确理解当前状态并完成协作；其次是减少重复上下文、重复读取和无效重试。不以整体压缩比例驱动改造，不因文字缩短就判定成功。

范围覆盖七个 Team 工具、Agent 通知、Member 动态 context、persona 与 core skills。有证据的行为问题可以修正，但行为变化与文案整理分别验证。保留七个工具的职责、权限、Attention 和 Task/Claim 语义；不改 Human Web Client 交互、不改 Harness 仓库、agent loop 或 shipped defaults。

工程细节由实施者决定：优先复用现有能力，选能够长期保留的最简单实现，不为假设需求引入通用框架、配置开关、备用实现或独立事实数据库。

## 2. 三个不同的状态

| 状态 | 含义 | 不意味着什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 当前上下文已提供某事实 | 来源和对象明确，必要内容完整出现在本次模型可用的上下文中 | 不等于模型理解正确，不等于持久已读 |
| 已确认已读 | 显式 `read` 确认的事实，由 Host 写入既有阅读状态 | 不等于事项完成，不改变 Attention |
| 操作已提交 | Host 按当前权限、状态及并发条件提交操作 | 不等于通知送达，不顺带清除未读 |

收到通知、发回复、`history`、`message` 查询和自动背景补充都不主动确认已读。`read` 可以省略当前上下文里已经完整提供的正文，但必须明确确认了哪些内容、哪些正文被省略、还有多少未读。

历史已读不会因压缩而撤销；压缩可能导致 Agent 缺少工作背景，需要重新提供。当前上下文中的完整性只是本次阅读条件的依据，不建立第二套持久未读状态。

## 3. Member 背景与记忆

- 新会话或上下文缺少起步背景时，提供当前身份、Project ownership、Workspace 参与及路径、预算内完整 memory 索引。
- 没有变化时不追加重复内容。

- memory 删除、不可读或超过既有预算时，明确异常及读取/维护入口，不继续把旧副本当成当前索引。

实施依据和 Harness interface 核对见 [工程核对](materials/2026-10-29-implementation-notes.md)。尤其注意：canonical 工具结果不自动持久化；当前 surface 中的最终文本才参与判断；裁剪后 `meta` 可能原样留下，不能只信 `meta`。复用 Session 记录，不建独立的已读事实库。

读取批次与确认需要在 Host 中协调。必要时增加窄的 Agent-owned 读取 interface，复用既有 Host 提交；不让 Session 可见性成为 ledger 重放的输入，不从 Agent renderer 更改 Human 读取行为。既有持久记录保持可重放，不为文案优化改变旧 operation 的解释。

现有公开 seam 不足时先记录具体限制再决定；不访问私有字段、不修改 Harness、不虚构已经存在的承诺。结构选择、字段、预算和内部测试由实施者决定，无需逐项交 Human 拍板。

## 9. 完整流程与验收

[六段完整流程](materials/2026-10-29-accepted-flows.md)是行为验收入口，不是仅比较措辞的 snapshot。

1. 起步、记忆更新、责任变化、压缩后恢复。
2. 普通更新、读取、理解当前分工、领取工作。
3. 直接提及、无需重复正文即可回复、稍后显式确认已读。
4. 旧状态写入被拒、收到完整变化、修改行动后提交。
5. 压缩后进入旧讨论、无未读也能恢复背景。
6. 长消息分段、可继续读取、完整后按动作性质确认。

实现检查使用真实累计的 Session surface；覆盖裁剪、压缩、重启、短正文、跨 Thread 同文、旧凭据、新消息并发、memory 异常及通知上限。只覆盖现实生命周期与公开输入，不为类型已保证的内部值叠防御测试。

模型评测复用既有 harness，使用隔离的合成场景，不上传个人会话语料；接入模型前核实本轮可用且获授权的配置，不复用归档中的凭据。关键指标是目标完成、根据新事实改行动、误调用与恢复次数，其后才是上下文 token/字符、总调用数与耗时。比较同一版本窗口和场景，重复运行并报告样本及波动，不承诺未测的成本比例。

## 10. 实施与完成条件

当前可开始的实施票为 01、02；其后按 [README 的依赖顺序](README.md#实施顺序)推进。每票包含行为、可见输出、测试及受影响正式文档，不先搭横向框架再等最后集成。

完成要求：六段流程成立；关键新事实不丢失；无无效凭据指引、错误确认或重复读取循环；模型评测不出现未解释的正确性回退；相关旧路径与矛盾规则删除；双语正式文档和 CHANGELOG 同步；仅在影响 assembled Web/Remote 等面时运行相应浏览器检查。

最初仅批准设计整理；2026-10-29 Human 随后授权推进生产实现，允许 subagent 实施、主线程审查。模型付费调用、提交和发布仍需另行授权。设计检查通过不等于上述实现验收通过。

# .scratch Work Rules

This subtree holds cross-session work items: design snapshots, research, implementation tickets, prototypes, and acceptance evidence. It is not an implementation or API authority — current behavior is defined by `packages/` source and tests, and maintenance rules by [`../docs/AGENTS.md`](../docs/AGENTS.md). This file only governs how to work here.

## Work-item structure

Each `active/<work>/` is one directory with a short `README.md` as its single continuation entry, covering five items: status, last-checked date, current frontier (who is doing what and what is blocked), completion conditions, and the formal-doc exit.

```
active/<work>/
├── README.md      # continuation entry (the five items above)
├── spec.md        # confirmed decision snapshot — written once discussion converges
├── issues/        # tracer-bullet implementation tickets, one file per ticket
│   ├── 01-<slug>.md
│   └── 02-<slug>.md
├── materials/     # research and external material (keep only what is worth re-reading)
└── validation/    # human-confirmed acceptance evidence (see the development doc)
```

## Ticket discipline

Each `issues/NN-<slug>.md` uses a fixed skeleton, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first):

```markdown
# NN — title

**What to build:** the end-to-end behavior this ticket demonstrably delivers once done (user perspective, not a layered task list)
**Blocked by:** the tickets blocking it, or "None — can start immediately"
**Status:** pending | ready | in-progress | complete

- [ ] acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] acceptance criterion 2
```

- **Vertical slices**: each ticket cuts one narrow, complete path through every layer (schema → API → UI → tests), independently verifiable when done; no horizontal division of labor by layer.
- **Self-contained tickets**: each ticket can start in a new context without reading the whole work-item history. Avoid concrete file paths and code snippets (they go stale); exception: decision-dense fragments from prototypes (state machines, type shapes) may be inlined with their source noted.
- **Frontier workflow**: tickets whose blockers are all done form the frontier and are ready to start; a serial chain runs top to bottom. Tickets that are written but still carry unfinished blockers stay **pending**, so `ready` always means startable now.
- **Wide-refactor exception**: when one mechanical change's blast radius covers the whole repository, do not force it into a tracer bullet — order it as expand–contract: expand first (old and new coexist), migrate in batches, then contract (delete the old form).

## Lifecycle

- **Closing a work item**: close or delete unfinished tickets → move durable conclusions into the `../docs/` maintained documents → delete process material without provenance value → move into `archive/YYYY-MM/`.
- **Archive is history**: archived states and terminology only represent the working context of their time and never override current implementation; do not rewrite archives to match new code.
- **Transient artifacts**: logs, debug screenshots, and downloads go in `local/` or `artifacts/` (gitignored), never into active or archive.

## Version control

- **Active does not enter version history**: while a work item is open, its `active/<work>/` directory is gitignored working material. Force-add it (`git add -f`) only when a reviewer must see it.
- **Archive enters history on close**: when a work item closes, move it into `archive/YYYY-MM/` and amend that move into the commit(s) that deliver the work, so the archive records what actually shipped instead of sitting in a scratch-only commit at the tip.

## Directory index

See [README.md](README.md).

# 六段已确认流程与验收矩阵

2026-10-29 Human 确认。下列中文是讨论用示例，不要求实现逐字翻译；标识符、数量、角色和事件均为合成数据，不代表实际 Team 状态。行为以 [spec](../spec.md) 为准。

## F1 起步、更新记忆、责任变化、压缩后恢复

```text
开始会话
  身份：@A，负责测试。
  Project ownership：无。
  Workspace：项目目录及读取入口。
  私有记忆：路径、用量、完整索引。

后续步骤无变化
  不再追加同样内容。

A 修改 memory.md
  索引已更新，先前副本不再代表最新文件；需要时按路径读取。

A 被授予项目 P 的 ownership
  ownership 当前列表：项目 P。
  不顺带重发 memory 或 Workspace。

压缩后缺少背景
  补当前身份、ownership、Workspace、最新完整 memory 索引。
  接上本次唤醒原因。
```

**检查**：无变化零重复注入；memory 变化不诱发每步重发；ownership 撤销为空、Workspace 多变一仍明确通知；提示残留而索引丢失时补完整索引；memory 缺失、不可读和超预算明确说明。

## F2 普通更新、读取、领取工作

```text
通知
  项目 P / Thread T 有 3 条普通更新，入口为 team_thread read。

read
  确认 3 条已读，剩余 0。
  主题：发布前兼容性验证。
  当前 Claim：@B 检查 Windows 安装。
  @B：Windows 安装由我负责。
  @human：还需要 Linux 回归。
  @C：Linux 环境已准备好。
  下一次写入凭据：由工具提供。

A 领取 Linux 回归
  Claim 已创建；负责人 A；方向 Linux 回归；active。
  说明本次建立的 Attention，返回新凭据。
```

**检查**：通知无普通正文；第一次 read 足以看到需求和当前分工；不重复 anchor；claim 结果不重放读到的正文；普通 Agent 不因 Team 改动获得这些工具或提示。

## F3 直接提及、直接回复、稍后确认已读

以 Main 为例。Thread 仍要求其既有写入凭据，不从通知猜数字。

```text
直接通知
  项目 P / Main，消息 M，@B：@A Linux 回归完成了吗？

前提
  当前上下文已有所需背景，没有其他缺失的必要事实。

A post 回复
  回归已完成，结果通过。
  工具：已提交，新消息 N，回复 M。
  M 未因通知或回复被确认已读。

稍后 read
  确认 M 已读；正文已在当前上下文中，不重复。
  如有新增 O，正常提供 O。
  说明剩余未读。
```

**检查**：post 不要求重新读取同一正文；没有写入后自动确认；未读可通过 read 清理且不重复正文；期间到达新消息不被顺带跳过。

## F4 旧状态写入被拒、重新判断、提交

```text
A 读完 Thread，准备留言“可以发布”。
B 随后发言：Windows 安装失败，先不要发布。

A 用旧凭据提交
  未提交，展示 B 的完整变化。
  相关变化已完整提供；要求重新考虑，给相应写入凭据。

A 修改行动
  先暂停发布。我来复现 Windows 安装问题。
  提交成功；无需再 read 同一句话。

稍后 read
  明确确认对应事实，已完整可见正文不重复。
```

**检查**：Agent 修改行动而非机械重试；结果与恢复句不冲突；拒绝只展示部分事实时要求继续读取；并发新消息仍重新检查；相同短正文、不同 Thread 不能误判；既有权限和关闭状态仍约束写入。

## F5 压缩后进入旧讨论，无未读也能恢复

```text
用户：继续处理那个安装问题。
A 定位 Thread 后 read。

没有未读，本次不改变未读状态。
主题：Windows 安装失败。
Task 进行中；A 负责复现；B 负责发布包。
近期原文：
  A：路径包含空格时失败。
  B：新版包已生成，等待复测。
更早历史未展示，可通过 history 读取。

A 根据需要直接复测，或查询原复现步骤。
```

**检查**：不因历史已读而只返空结果；不重放全部历史；不额外调用模型摘要；没有新已读 operation；背景查询不改变 Attention；再次 read 且背景仍在时不继续堆副本。

## F6 长消息、分段续读、确认范围一致

```text
通知
  B 提及 A，正文较长；当前只给预览和读取入口。

# 合成场景与上下文量测

当前行为以 packages 源码与测试为准；本目录为工作项的验收工具，不读取个人 Session，也不调用真实模型。

## 当前组合场景

从仓库根运行：

```bash
npx vitest run --config .scratch/active/agent-tools-context-rendering/harness/vitest.config.ts --project context-scenarios
```

使用既有 realHarness、ScriptedAdapter 和真实 Agent loop，在同一 Session 中依次验证 F3（direct→post→read）、F5（压缩→无未读背景恢复→不重复）与 F6（长通知→message续读→显式确认），同时检查 Host 未读状态。F1、F2、F4 与更多边界复用 packages 下现有集成测试，定位见 `../materials/2026-10-30-acceptance-plan.md`。

输出 `.scratch/local/agent-context-implementation/context-snapshots.json`。它是合成场景快照，不是 Session 存储文件格式；不要传入个人日志。

## 当前量测

```bash
node --import tsx .scratch/active/agent-tools-context-rendering/harness/context-volume.mts .scratch/local/agent-context-implementation/context-snapshots.json
```

必须显式指定输入，不会默认扫描本机目录。可以传多个合成快照文件，分别列出文件数量、Session 数量及每个阶段。

- `cumulativeLog`：截至该检查点的全部已记录文本，按工具动作与 Member 背景类别分别计数。包括已经离开当前上下文的内容。
- `currentSurface`：通过 Harness 的 Session 投影得到的当前模型上下文文本。
- `requests`：真实 Agent loop 交给 ScriptedAdapter 的每次 GenerateOptions；文本、消息 JSON 和工具 schema JSON 分开计数。realHarness 的测试preset不包含完整发布persona，所以不是生产请求总长度或provider网络请求字节数。
- `partBindings` / `wholeMessageBindings`：输出中记录的分段／全文绑定次数，不代表唯一内容量或当前仍可见的内容量。

所有长度都是 UTF-16 代码单元，不是 token、费用或模型理解质量。每个检查点在自身 Session 内累计，不可把连续检查点相加。该工具通过实际 Session 的恢复验证事件和 surface，不从 metadata 单独推断可见事实。

## Member 分类更新对比

```bash
node --import tsx .scratch/active/agent-tools-context-rendering/harness/member-context-scenario.mts
```

固定合成 memory 与责任变化，对比基线 `deaa671` 和当前实现。每个版本独立 Session，分别输出单步注入、完整索引副本和当前 surface 字符数。

## 历史工具

`member-context-resend.mjs` 与 `member-context-triggers.mjs` 是旧个人日志研究入口，不属于当前验收命令，不应默认重跑。原 `context-volume.mjs` 的自动扫描实现已由上述显式合成输入工具替代；历史材料中的数字和命令保留原记录，不更新成新结果。

## 真实模型

ScriptedAdapter 固定行为，只证明组合和状态规则，不证明模型会正确理解。旧 `team-tools-model-eval` runner 自行拼 messages、直接 execute/render，适合历史参数形状评测，但不能验证本工作项的 Session 上下文恢复。真实模型验收应继续复用真实 Agent loop；运行前确认本轮模型配置和费用授权，不复制归档配置或凭据。

# 工程核对与旧方案替代关系

日期：2026-10-29。Team HEAD 为 `3d16926`；工作副本中 `package.json`、Host `index.ts` 和性能基准脚本有其他工作项改动，本轮没有修改。Harness 相邻源码的 package 版本为 `0.2.1-rc.2`，与 Team 声明的范围相符；未运行安装或构建，不能据此声称已认证全部运行时能力。

本文记录设计阶段查到的事实和实施顺序，不是已实现方案。行为决定以 [spec](../spec.md) 为准。

## 1. 已核对的公开能力

| 需求 | 当前能力与证据 | 实施结论 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 获取当前模型可见内容 | Harness `Session.surface.nodes`、`snapshotEvents`、`deriveEventMessage`；`packages/core/session/src/index.ts` | 从当前 surface 派生，读取应用了投影的消息；不扫描全日志当成当前上下文 |
| 识别 Team 通知 | Team `context-source.ts`、`member-context.ts`、`surface-visibility.ts`；Harness `MessageSourceMap` 可扩展 | 复用 producer attribution；如需附事实标识，放在 Team 自有声明中，不修改 Harness |
| 核对工具返回 | Harness `tool/result` 有最终 `message` 与可选 `meta`；调用由 callId 关联 `tool/call` | canonical value 不持久化，不能假设能从日志读回原始 structured result |
| 工具输出阶段 | Harness `ToolOutputDefinition.render/presentationMeta`，`projectContent/finalizeContent` | 输出内容与 metadata 不等同于最终模型看到的内容；不用展示 metadata 单独证明完整性 |
| 裁剪后的事实识别 | `compaction-tool-result-pruner` 重写 content，但复制原事件其余字段 | meta 保留不表示正文保留；当前投影文本与具体事实均须对应 |
| pre-step 注入 | `PreStepDecision` 提供 `messages: UserMessage[]`，不提供 producer-local replace 指令 | 采用分类增量注入；不把“每步替换原块”写成已经验证的能力 |
| Thread 已读提交 | Team `prepareReadReceiptFrom` 与 `validateThreadReadReceipt` 当前重放同一批次规则 | 不能直接修改固定批次导致旧 receipt 重放不一致；新 Agent 选择要有可持久重放的精确范围 |
| Main 已读提交 | Team `readMainStream` 支持 readThroughSequence，默认未读分批；`mainReadPage` 提供最近页和被消费旧标记 | Agent 展示策略不能先确认后裁剪；保留 Human Remote 现有读取行为 |
| 单消息读取 | `AgentTeamReadMessageRequest` 仅接受身份，无片段游标；`readMessage` 返回完整 body | 分段续读不是现成能力；在现有 `team_thread` 内补窄 interface，不新建第八个工具 |

关键源码入口（均按函数名定位，避免依赖后续漂移的行号）：

- Team：`packages/agent-team/src/member-context.ts`、`surface-visibility.ts`、`ledger.ts` 的 `prepareReadReceiptFrom`、`prepareReadFrom`、`mainReadPage`、`deferredThreadWrite`；`packages/tool-agent-team/src/index.ts` 的 `rejectionLines` 与 `teamThread`。
- Harness：`packages/core/session/src/types.ts` 的 `tool/result`；`packages/core/session/src/index.ts` 的 `deriveEventMessage`；`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts` 的 `ToolOutputDefinition` 和 `ToolExecutionSuccess`；`packages/compaction/compaction-tool-result-pruner/src/index.ts` 的 `pruneSession`；`packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts` 的 `PreStepDecision`。

## 2. 采用的实现方向

### 2.1 当前可见事实

扩展已有 surface visibility module 的内部 interface，而不是创建单独的“已读事实数据库”。一次操作读取当前 surface 并复用结果，不为每条事实重扫整段会话。

对工具结果，使用 Team 工具身份、已持久化的内容及具体事实身份核对。对通知，复用 Team producer 和结构化来源。只有完整的、可对应的内容才供阅读检查和省略正文使用；模型自己写的文本不参与。

事实标识如何与片段绑定由实施者在票 02 的真实 Session 测试里收敛。优先现有日志字段；确有需要时只添加窄的 Team 自有记录。不可用工具展示 metadata 或正文模糊包含代替完整性，也不加入 durable mirror 或恢复兼容分支。摘要不视为原文。

### 2.2 注入和缺失背景

分类识别当前可见的 identity、ownership、Workspace、memory 基线及后续更新。用现有 source 的 Team-owned 字段或当前块识别，不先建设通用 context registry。memory 提示与完整基线是两类事件；提示残留不能证明基线仍在。

压缩与恢复使用当前 surface，因此无须维护独立的跨会话“曾读过”状态。已有持久已读不因上下文被压缩而回退。

### 2.3 读取选择和确认

保留 Host 权威。读取先选择可完整交付的批次与片段，再提交相应阅读范围；Agent 结果根据同一选择渲染。已在当前上下文完整提供的内容可被计入确认范围但省略正文。额外背景不主动改变未读。

Thread 当前读 receipt 的重放按固定规则重新推导；改变批次必须同时设计新记录的确定性表示和重放测试，不能把 Session surface 写进 replay 依赖。保留既有历史记录的含义，不引入双套运行时读取策略。Main 复用已有序列上界，不因方便而修改 Human Client 的默认页。

### 2.4 长消息续读

复用 `team_thread` 的 read/message，使用系统给出的续读值推进不可变消息正文。默认普通消息仍全文，超长才分段。具体游标形式、单位和额度由实施者决定，不暴露 offset 与 limit 等多套等价选择。

读到末段不自动证明前段仍完整可见；缺段时明确补读，不误确认。正常连续续读必须有进展。若单条大到无法在模型容量内完整提供，应明确报出这个实际限制和读取入口，不声称“已完整读取”；不得为极端长度预建通用大文件或事务框架。

## 3. 旧方案替代关系

旧提案、度量脚本和契约盘点保留为历史证据；原五张票已原样移至 [旧票据目录](2026-10-29-superseded-tickets/01-memory-injection-strategy.md)。它们的 ready/complete 是当时状态，不是当前前沿。

| 原项目 | 新决定 |
| --- | --- |
| 01 两类摘要、非 memory 变化重发整块、保留备用策略 | 分类更新；不随 ownership 重发 memory；不保留另一套注入策略 |
| 02 “render 已落、gate 未落，因此不是设计取舍” | 确认行为变化：来源明确且完整的事实可满足阅读条件；不保证重试提交，跨 Thread/Main/Activity 一致 |
| 03 仅改 Main Agent renderer、只返未读与主题行 | 改为读取选择与确认一致，同时补讨论恢复背景；不得先确认后裁剪 |
| 04 逐工具盘点已 complete | 保留为历史清单，不能作为新行为验收完成 |
| 05 每条规则只出现一次 | 单一规则定义，允许必要位置短提醒；通过实际模型调用验证 |
| memory 累计字符下降至少 80% | 不再是整体完成门槛；同场景测量重复减少，同时以行为正确为先 |
| 先建共享语义层 | 不建；只提取已存在真实调用者的共享完整性/渲染逻辑 |

原始 [SCOPE](../SCOPE.md) 已标为历史；[旧提案](2026-10-28-baseline-and-proposal.md)及[契约盘点](2026-10-29-seven-tools-contract-inventory.md)正文不重写。

## 4. 验证约束

设计阶段只检查文档、链接、票据依赖及引用事实，不把它算作运行验收。实现先跑窄的 Host/tool/Session 组合测试，再按影响面跑类型、正式文档和构建检查；涉及 Remote 或 assembled Web 时必须 browser 验证。

旧语料是滚动增长的历史日志，累计字符不是单次上下文占用或真实费用。复跑需要固定输入窗口、区分 session 与日志文件、读取 surface 替换与压缩。原脚本保留不表示测量方法已支持新注入/分段格式。

参考成熟工具实践：[Writing effective tools for agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents)。采用其有意义结果、分页、可执行恢复和真实场景评测原则，不把示例 token 节省率当成本项目收益。

7	export async function readingCapacity(agent: Agent, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<number> {

57	/** Select exactly the renderable prefix before the Host acknowledges it. Repeated calls fill the first gap on the live surface. */

59	  const surface = visibleTeamSurface(agent)

73	      ...(value.kind !== 'read' ? {} : { remainingUnreadCount: (value.remainingUnreadCount ?? 0) + unread.length - acknowledged,

80	    candidate = make(selected)
81	  }

83	    selected = [background[0]!]

93	    const target = { ...address, messageRef: first.messageRef, body: first.body }

108	  if (!fits(candidate)) throw new Error('A single fact or its required context exceeds the fixed reading output budget; nothing acknowledged. Activity events cannot be split. 101	      else high = end - 1

106	    candidate = make(selected, [{ messageRef: first.messageRef, start, end, complete: complete(end) }])
107	  }
108	  if (!fits(candidate)) throw new Error('A single fact or its required context exceeds the fixed reading output budget; nothing acknowledged. Activity events cannot be split. Repeating this call or changing models cannot remove this limit; ask the Human to inspect the event and decide how to continue.')

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index ddd5dd4..1666334 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -15,6 +15,7 @@ All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format foll
 - Responsibility events reach the Inbox as direct facts regardless of Attention: being made accountable, entering review, a Task left unowned, reopen, and needs-your-acceptance when the accountable owner executed the work.
 - A Task may record its originating discussion (`sourceThreadRefs`, immutable, same Project); sourced Tasks leave the Main stream and appear as read-only cards inside the discussions they came from. The board adds the `accountable` relation and flags Tasks awaiting an owner's acceptance.
 - `team_task` gains `accept`, `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer`; `team_message.start` accepts an accountable owner and source discussions for Tasks. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill state the accountable/verifier split.
+- The team-member persona separates naming from mentioning: a Member referred to in plain prose — Iris, Ferry — is a reference, while `@Handle` in a Message body is a delivery, so a stray `@` inside a roster explanation or a quoted report no longer interrupts Members who need not act on it.
 - Notices are delivered by Attention. Every unread fact interrupts: a Main stream post, a new discussion, mentions, replies, ownership events, responsibility events and Task reminders wake immediately, and so does an ordinary Thread update for any Member following that Thread. The former owner and accountable threshold — five ordinary Thread updates per Member per Thread before a summary — is gone, so following a Thread now means being interrupted by its first ordinary update, and no identity places a reader in a slower class. The sender's own messages never enter the sender's Inbox.
 - A Main stream commit wakes every Member whose Main stream Attention covers that stream, not only the Project's owners, so a non-owner follower is interrupted by the first ordinary update like anyone else. Following a Main stream requires Project membership, exactly as reading and writing it do, so an Attention row left behind by a departed Member delivers nothing and the follow cannot be the door that gets a Member in.
 - An ownership grant no longer overwrites the Main stream Attention a Member already holds: a Member that followed and read before being granted ownership keeps its own read watermark, so granting ownership no longer silently clears its unread. The Human's own row is derived from owning the Project, so a Main stream unfollow from the Human is refused instead of committing an operation that changes nothing; `team_attention` takes `projectRef` or a Thread ref, never both, at the Host as well as the tool.
@@ -30,7 +31,15 @@ All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format foll
 
 **Changed**
 
+- Agent Thread and Main stream reads restore missing original discussion context even after compaction with no unread. Already-visible Message bodies are explicitly omitted while the read acknowledges the same chronological batch; background, Main stream Thread cards, and current Task cards remain separate from newly acknowledged facts. Human reads and historical read receipts are unchanged.
+- Agent `read` and `message` results share one output ceiling: the tool selects fewer facts, an oversized Message body returns in ordered parts, a read acknowledges only the prefix it can deliver and never crosses an incomplete Message, and repeating the same request resumes at the first missing segment of the current Session surface. A Thread read receipt records the selected bound, while receipts written before it keep the default batch; there is no offset parameter.
+- Complete Thread Message rejections provide the facts and current token needed to reconsider a write without a mandatory extra read. The Host verifies exact Team source, Thread/Message identity, and the actual Session text; summaries and truncated results cannot satisfy the check. Partial rejections supply no token, and neither notifications nor rejections acknowledge unread work.
+- Task and Claim Activities follow the same context rule as Messages. A notice, read/history result, or rejection binds the immutable event — actor, object, and recorded Claim refs or transfer endpoints — never current Task or Claim state; a complete mixed Message/Activity rejection supplies the Thread token, while partial facts do not. A Main stream post has no token and accepts complete pending entries from the current Session or an explicit read, and new unread entries, revision, permissions, and Task state are checked again.
+- An Activity already fully visible in the current context is acknowledged by identity only, with its event marked as already present; the repeated identity does not bind a second time. An Activity is one line and cannot be split, so one beyond the output ceiling acknowledges nothing and reports that limit instead of offering continuation.
+- Agent notices prioritize missing direct Messages and responsibility changes across Threads and the Main stream. Complete facts already in the current Session use short identities without repeating their bodies or creating another binding; replies retain their target. Scope and detail caps apply after ranking, and the whole notice including recovery instructions stays within one character budget. Omitted direct signals and Task reminders retain an explicit count and bounded reading routes. Main counts name their Project, and another Member's ownership change is counted without telling the reader they became an owner. Delivery, unread counts, and markers are unchanged.
+- Member context updates identity, Project ownership, Workspace participation, and private memory separately. Editing `memory.md` produces a short stale-copy notice instead of repeating the full index and unrelated background; missing context restores the relevant current blocks. Empty ownership and reduced Workspace participation remain explicit.
 - The Team settings nav row now carries the Team mark instead of the shell's generic gear. The shell draws nav glyphs by section id and `settings.section` offers no icon, so the row is tagged inside the settings dialog and the mark is painted over the shell glyph with a mask — the same contained workaround installed third-party themes use; it releases itself on dispose.
+- The composer's mention picker is rebuilt on the version 2 model instead of the retired version 1 one. Its order no longer claims to rank how directly a pick reaches a Member — every mention is now a durable direct marker delivered identically whether or not the recipient follows, and the invitation step that once made a non-follower slower is gone. Rows are grouped by relation on `data-mention-group`: Project owners first (pinned, so the Members who decide are always at hand), then this Thread's followers, then the rest of the Project, then Workspace peers a pick would enroll into the Project — because a mention of a non-member is a Project-membership fact, and the recipient notice now names those Members as joining before the send. Within a group the order is online first, then handle, so it no longer drifts with the roster's arrival order. An offline Member is no longer dropped — a durable mention waits for them — so only lifecycle (`inactive`/`archived`) ends eligibility. A typed query now matches a handle substring or a description keyword, and an empty result shows a 「没有匹配的成员」 line instead of closing the popup.
 - The Client drops its version 1 paths: the old Project feed, `@all` expansion, and the invitation confirmation flow are gone. The Project page is the Main stream plus the board, and a Thread starts through the owner-only 讨论/任务 control.
 - Exactly one sidebar row carries `aria-current="page"`: a global face (Inbox, Task board) no longer leaves the marker on the Workspace selector beneath it, and the auto-select no longer pulls the seat back to a Workspace overview while a global face stands.
 - A Message's row actions stay on the Message they act on. The copy/quote card still floats at its row's top-right corner, but it is anchored to that row instead of to a rise measured upwards out of it: the rise put the card in the band the row above owns, so a Message that opens a run showed its actions over the empty gutter of the Message before it. A run head now hangs its card beside its own author line, clear of the first words by the row's own padding plus that line minus the card's height, and a continuation still rises over its run's own previous line; the Thread timeline no longer reserves the rise, so the first row of a page keeps its inset.
@@ -40,9 +49,11 @@ All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format foll
 - The Thread page's follow, transfer, accept, close, and reopen controls render as one action band of two groups separated by a 1px rule, instead of four sibling containers spread across the header. Every control in the band shares one 28px height, one radius, one 10px inline inset, one outlined stroke and one 6px step; widths stay content-sized. The followed state now paints the shipped selected fill (the ghost-active vocabulary `Pill` and `ClockPicker` already use) instead of reading as an unfollowed button with a different word. Visible verbs shorten to 关注/取消关注/转交 while the accessible names keep the full phrases and take the long pending phrase while a write runs, so the shorter word never leaves the write unannounced. That band's failures are one 12px line per refusing control under the band rather than the whole-surface `errorState`, and a committed transfer states the new accountable beside the control, retiring the line once the projection moves on.
 - Mentions and replies are delivered from the message body alone: the `@Handle` names in a body, plus the quoted Message's author on a reply, are the whole recipient set for both the Web Client and `team_message`. The request no longer carries a separate `recipients` list, so a composer's notice and the Host's delivery read the same set.
 - Maintained documentation and the shipped `agent-team` README no longer describe rules version 1 as current. Corrected: a Main stream message creates no Thread (`startThread` does); a mention or reply never starts or resumes Attention; `@all` is plain text; the invitation confirmation step is version 1 only; an owner's ordinary Main stream unread is delivered immediately; the request's explicit `recipients` list is stated as the input it is, unioned with the body's mentions, rather than denied; and `changeAttention` is recorded as a Host Remote the Web Client does not yet wire, instead of a control the Human Client is claimed to use. Bilingual pairs moved together.
+- Seven-tool guidance now follows one placement rule: the persona carries cross-tool rules, each tool description the contract its selection and call need, results this operation's state and recovery, and `team-domain-model` the detailed method. `team_attention` states that a Thread and the Main stream are mutually exclusive addresses while `threadRef` and its `taskRef` alias may travel together for the same Thread, and `team_thread message` requires `threadRef` or `projectRef`. Recovery wording is described as the registry for faults that have a route, not as a guarantee that every rejection has a next step.
 
 **Fixed**
 
+- The rules-version-1 undelivered-mention result is no longer shown to models: it survives only as the Host's historical explanation when replaying a version-1 ledger. Maintained documentation no longer describes a `replyToMessageRef` settings switch that does not exist.
 - The follow control reads the Human's own row out of the follower set instead of asking whether the set is non-empty. The set holds every Member whose Attention is on the Thread, so while any Agent still followed, the Human's unfollow left the button pressed with the pressed fill while its word read 「关注」; the same reading also made a press on a Thread only an Agent followed answer "already following". The Human's own Attention and notification gate were never wrong — only the Client's identity test was.
 - Every whole-surface loading state renders one box in one place. /** Durable content of one Thread read: the watermark advanced to and the Inbox delta consumed. Everything else the read answered with is derived from the projection at read time and on replay. */
export interface AgentTeamThreadReadReceipt {
  readonly workspaceId: WorkspaceId
  readonly memberId: AgentTeamMemberId
  readonly threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef
  readonly taskRef?: AgentTeamTaskRef | undefined
  readonly readThroughSequence: number
  /**
   * The Host-selected prefix bound this read acknowledged, when the caller
   * bounded one. It is not the watermark: replay re-derives the acknowledged
   * batch from the projection plus this bound. Absent means the default batch,
   * which also keeps every older receipt's meaning.
   */
  readonly selectedThroughSequence?: number | undefined
  readonly inbox: AgentTeamInboxDelta
}

export interface AgentTeamThreadReadSnapshot {
  readonly workspaceId: WorkspaceId
  readonly memberId: AgentTeamMemberId
  readonly task?: AgentTeamTask | undefined
  readonly thread: AgentTeamThread
  readonly claims: readonly AgentTeamClaim[]
  readonly anchor: AgentTeamStoredMessage
  /** Structured Member refs of the anchor Message, from its originating send operation. */
  readonly anchorMentions: readonly AgentTeamMemberId[]
  readonly facts: readonly AgentTeamStoredThreadReadFact[]
  readonly readThroughSequence: number
  readonly remainingUnreadCount: number
  readonly attention?: AgentTeamThreadAttention | undefined
  readonly inbox: AgentTeamInboxDelta
}

/** Both durable Thread-read forms: the receipt every new read writes, and the legacy snapshot. */
export type AgentTeamThreadReadData = AgentTeamThreadReadReceipt | AgentTeamThreadReadSnapshot

/** Durable one-batch read and direct-marker consumption. It does not revise the Thread. */
export interface AgentTeamThreadReadOperation extends AgentTeamOperationBase {
  readonly kind: 'team/thread-read'

Thread 侧：`previewThreadRead` 只有 2 行，`readThread` 里的重复是 `assertActorForWorkspace` + `prepareRead`。这是很轻的重复——`assertActorForWorkspace` 是必须的（校验），`prepareRead` 被调用两次但参数不同（一次无 selection 用于 preview，一次带 selection）。

content.text:
优化完成。

## 改了什么

**1. 三处重复的 rejection meta 合成** → 抽成 `rejectionMeta()`

`team_message` 有两处、`team_task` 有一处，都是 `{ kind, teamFacts: teamMessageSurface(rendered.text, rendered.messages, rendered.activities) }`。现在三处都调同一个函数。类型用 `Parameters<typeof teamMessageSurface>` 推导，不用把 Host 的内部类型拉到工具包来。

**2. Main 读取的重复推导** → 抽成 `planMainRead()`

`readMainStream` 和 `previewMainStreamRead` 各写了一遍 `mainHeadFrom` → backlog 取页 → `readThrough` 校验 → `prepareMainReadFrom`。现在共用一个私有 planner，返回 `readThrough`、`inbox`、`noOp`、`consumed`。两边的差别（一个要写 operation、一个只出 picture）留在各自的调用处。

**3. 三个无调用者的导出** → 收窄成本模块内

`READ_MAX_CHARACTERS`、`isActivityOnSurface`、`renderMemberMemoryUpdate` 都只在本文件内使用，去掉 `export`。`renderMemberMemoryState` 和 `renderMemberMemoryUpdate` 的 `privateMemoryPath` 默认值也去掉——唯一调用点都显式传参。`renderMemberMemory` 的默认值保留，测试在用。

## 撤回一条

审查说的"`activityFact` 联合重载无调用者"**不成立**。我实测删掉它：

```
packages/agent-team/tests/surface-probe.spec.ts(86,29): error TS2769: No overload matches this call.
```

`surface-probe.spec.ts` 的 `activityResult` helper 参数是 `AgentTeamActivity | AgentTeamMainActivity`，走的就是联合重载。它是真实使用者，删了测试直接报类型错。已恢复。

## 验证

| 检查 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `vitest` 全量 | 133 files / 1507 tests 通过，1 原有跳过 |
| `typecheck` | 只剩性能工作项那 2 个既有错误（`post-commit-delivery.spec.ts:214,230`） |
| `lint` | 回到原有 2 条 ledger warning，**无新增** |
| `check:docs` / `core-skills` / `boundaries` / `comments` | 全部通过 |
| `jscpd` | clone 11 → 9，重复行 95 → 80，重复 token 967 → 833 |

全量测试从 1506 涨到 1507 是性能工作项那个新测试——之前我 stash 掉性能改动跑基线时它不在，恢复后就跑起来了。不是本次改动加的测试。

## 还剩一项没做

`team_message` 和 `team_task` 的 `presentationMeta` 还有一对 jscpd clone（返回类型注解 + `renderRejection(value).text` 尾行，8 行 66 token）。这是两个不同工具的自然形状，抽它要按工具参数化一个间接层。按审查自己排除同类项的标准（"收益小于复杂度"），我没动。

另外那两个提交的 `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer 需要改历史。那是 Entire CLI 的 `prepare-commit-msg` hook 自动加的，不是手写——要处理得先关 hook 再 reword，而且 `805394f` 是 master 的 tip。这个动历史的事我没擅自动，等你说。

还有两路审查（Spec、Correctness）没回来。

## 沟通规范

- 说人话，拒绝行业黑话、互联网黑话。
- 简洁优先。
- 只问真正需要用户拍板的问题。
- 模仿用户的表达方式。

## 文档与报告写作规范

适用于结构化文档与报告（故障报告、分析、清单等）；日常对话遵循“沟通规范”。

- 使用标准术语；已有通用说法时直接采用。
- 直接陈述，让读者无需推断指代对象；用字面表述代替比喻。
- 表头和分类名使用中性名词，如“问题”“现象”“影响”“结果”。
- 直接陈述结论或定义。
- 表格条目按需填写，说明发生了什么即可；数字和结论在有把握时给出。
- 未查明原因的问题写“原因未查明”。
- 使用正式、客观的表述。

## UI / UX 改动

- 涉及界面或交互改动时，用 ASCII UI 展示示意。

## 向用户汇报

用简单直白的语言说清楚：做了什么、结果怎样。

- 把术语和技术细节转成日常语言。
- 像在跟一个聪明人解释，对方没在看代码。
- 干活过程怎么都行；这条要求只针对汇报方式。

## 自验

在汇报前，先用实际工具验证工作结果：

- 能运行就运行，检查输出。
- Web 类：打开页面走一遍流程，确认渲染和交互正常。
- 脚本：拿真实输入跑，检查结果。
- 边界情况也试一遍。

发现问题就先修好，交付能用的成果，让用户拿到就能用。

## 完成标准

- 动手前先想清楚：任务做到什么程度才算完成。
- 先给自己列检查清单。
- 只有确认一切正常，或者真的遇到需要用户介入的障碍，才来找用户。

## 工具使用偏好

- 涉及 GitHub 的操作（查源码、读文件、发 API 请求、查 PR/Issue）优先用 `gh`。

## 方案与决策默认规则

- 默认追求在当前目标和约束下长期最优、完整、干净的最终方案；在充分满足需求的前提下采用尽可能简单的实现，抽象、配置项和间接层只在有实际需求依据时引入。
- 废弃的代码路径直接移除，连同兼容层、回退机制和迁移方案一并清理；旧接口、旧行为、旧结构只在用户明确要求时保留。替换时一次迁移到位，保持单一实现并存。
- 架构决策着眼长期演进，采用可长期承载的方案；提出的方案应是可长期保留的最终形态。
- 在自行实现或新增依赖之前，先评估项目现有依赖的能力：查阅相关文档和类型定义，确认其是否已具备所需能力。成熟且维护良好的库能降低整体复杂度或提高可靠性时优先采用，通用功能直接复用既有实现。
- 在设计解决方案之前，先研究成熟产品如何解决同类问题，优先采用经过验证的模式和约定。
- 采用渐进式、分层的方式构建系统：先完成能够端到端运行的最小版本，再基于稳定可用的产品逐步增加功能。保持组件模块化，明确划分不同职责与关注点。
- 需求、约束、意图、边界不清时，先问清楚再动手。长期最优方案和时间压力、现有约束冲突时，直接说清冲突点，再让用户确认。

## Memory / Nowledge Mem

把 `nmem` / Nowledge Mem 当作你和用户共同的长期记忆系统。它服务于协作连续性，沉淀跨会话有用的结论和上下文。

### 基本分工

- `Profile`：用户是谁、长期偏好、全局协作方式。
- `Space`：当前工作场景 / 项目 / agent lane。只有长期上下文会互相干扰时才建；方法类工作（调研、排障、写作、总结）留在 Default。
- `Working Memory`：某个 space 今天/近期最该记住的重点。会话开始或接续任务时优先读一次；同一会话读一次即可。
- `Memory`：一条长期有用的结论，写“决定了什么 + 为什么”。
- `Thread`：原始对话或 handoff。需要原文历史时查 thread；只要结论时查 memory。
- `Library`：原始资料、文档、网页、文件。资料保整体，结论再提炼成 memory。
- `Label / unit-type`：记忆类型和筛选方式，例如 `decision`、`procedure`、`preference`、`incident`、`current-state`、`historical`。label 只管记忆类型筛选，领域隔离交给 space。

### 什么时候搜索

- 做延续性任务、复盘、架构取舍、偏好判断、调试排障、相似问题前，先想是否该搜 memory。
- 用户提到“之前、上次、那个方案、为什么这样定”时，主动搜。
- 默认先搜 memory；如果用户问原始讨论、完整历史、某次对话细节，再搜 thread。

### 2.1 必须保持的三状态

完整通知、read/history/message 结果、完整拒绝可以满足当前上下文条件，但：
- 通知／查询／回复成功不推进已读水位。
- 不消费未读 marker。
- 只有显式 read 确认。
- 每次写仍检查新事实、权限、Thread revision、Task 状态及验收资格。
- Main 不新增 Thread token。
- 当前 board/card 状态不证明历史 Activity 或对应 Thread 已读。

### 2.2 架构

- Team 是外部 opt-in Cordis bundle。
- `packages/agent-team` 唯一 Team authority。
- append-only ledger 是持久事实来源。
- `packages/tool-agent-team` 七个模型工具只通过隔离 `team-member` preset。
- Human 只有 Web Client 控制面。
- 不改相邻 Harness、agent loop、默认行为。
- 不新增第二套持久已读状态、通用上下文框架、通知数据库或兼容 fallback。

七工具：
`team_view`、`team_inbox`、`team_attention`、`team_thread`、`team_message`、`team_dm`、`team_task`。

### 2.3 当前 Session 完整事实判断

`packages/agent-team/src/surface-visibility.ts`

- SHA-256 绑定生产者实际完整输出文本。
- Message 绑定 Thread 或 Main Project、messageRef、bodyDigest；分段还带 start/end/total。
- Activity 绑定 immutable event 的身份及 factDigest。
- 只从当前 `session.surface.nodes` 派生的实际文本判断。
- Team notice 要正确 producer 和 `form:'notice'`。
- tool result 沿 `sourceEventSeqs` 找到同 callId 的真实 Team tool call。
- 通过 `deriveEventMessage(event)` 校验实际文本 digest。
- 文本裁掉但 metadata 保留，不算完整。
- 没有 substring、模型复述或“我看过”备用判断。
- identity-only／省略结果不能重新绑定被省略全文。
- queued notice 尚未进入 surface，不算可见。

已实现读取：
- read/message 总输出上限 32768 UTF-16 code units。
- 重复同请求从当前 surface 最早缺段继续，无 offset 参数。
- 一批过长先减条数，单 Message 仍过长才分段。
- read 完整覆盖才确认，不能越过未完整旧 Message。
- message 始终不确认。
- Activity 不分段，超过固定输出上限明确不确认并交 Human。
- history 仍 count-only 分页，未承诺总字符预算。

# 合成场景与上下文量测

当前行为以 packages 源码与测试为准；本目录为工作项的验收工具，不读取个人 Session，也不调用真实模型。

## 当前组合场景

从仓库根运行：

```bash
npx vitest run --config .scratch/active/agent-tools-context-rendering/harness/vitest.config.ts --project context-scenarios

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /home/yu/.claude/skills/skill-manager

# Skill Manager

A skill preserves a reusable way of working. It is not a memory, a personal preference, or a record of one event.

## Decide

Create or revise a skill when the method has been demonstrated in real work and will make later work clearer or more reliable. Keep one-off work, changing facts, and personal continuity in their ordinary notes.

## Create Or Install

A skill is a directory named `<skill-name>/` containing `SKILL.md`. The location that matters is the directory the current harness discovers skills from; common conventions:

| Harness | Global | Project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pi | `~/.pi/agent/skills/` | `.pi/skills/` (project root) |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/` | `.claude/skills/` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/skills/` | — |

"Install" means creating or copying the directory into the chosen root; no registration command is needed. When unsure where the current harness looks, check its docs before placing files; if the target harness or scope is ambiguous, ask the user. For the Pi harness, install globally under `~/.pi/agent/skills/` unless the user asks for a project-local skill.

When skills are maintained in a source repository, prefer installing by symlink rather than by copy — copies drift stale as the repository evolves:

```bash
ln -s /abs/path/to/repo/skills/<group>/<skill-name> ~/.pi/agent/skills/<skill-name>
```

Harnesses follow the link and read the live files, so one repository update reaches every harness at once. Re-create links only when a skill is added, renamed, or moved.

Keeping several roots in step by hand does not scale; run `scripts/sync_installs.py` (beside this file) to sync them in one pass. It adds links for new skills, relinks moved ones, and removes links to retired ones. It manages only links that resolve into this repository: plain directories and foreign symlinks are reported and left alone, and a same-named stale copy is swapped for the repository link only under `--replace-copies` (`--dry-run` previews every action).

Use a short lowercase hyphenated name. Keep the directory name and the `name` field the same.

```md
---
name: skill-name
description: What this skill does and when to use it.
---
```

Declare the invocation kind in frontmatter: omit `disable-model-invocation` for model-invoked, or set it to `true` for user-invoked (see [Skill Mechanics](references/skill-mechanics.md)).

Read an offered skill before adopting it. Do not write harness-specific install paths into a skill body that must stay portable; state location conventions only when the skill is inherently about installation.

## Write

Describe the method the next Agent needs, not general advice it already knows. Make the description name the real triggers. Keep the main instructions short. Put substantial scripts, references, or templates beside `SKILL.md` only when they are repeatedly useful.

Use clear completion checks for fragile work. For a substantial new or revised skill, read [Writing Great Skills](references/writing-great-skills.md) for the writing methodology (the two loads, pointers, information hierarchy, leading words, pruning) and [Skill Mechanics](references/skill-mechanics.md) for frontmatter, the invocation choice, splitting, and this repository's index rules.

## Review

Read the finished skill once. Check that its name, description, directory, and method agree, and that no existing skill already owns the same method or name.

Writing or changing a skill does not add tools, credentials, permissions, or external services. Harnesses scan skill locations at startup: the current session keeps its existing skill list, and a later session discovers the change.

## Configuration and credentials

A skill that needs an API key, token, or other secret keeps it in its own `auth.json` (JSON, one file per skill) and reads it from there at run time; it does not put the secret in `SKILL.md`, scripts, messages, or other persisted text. Non-secret settings live in `config.json` beside it. Document the exact read/use convention in the skill's `SKILL.md` (file names, expected JSON shape, and how scripts consume them). When installing or creating a skill, follow the same layout and reference it in the skill's `SKILL.md`. See [Configuration and Credentials for Skills](references/auth-and-config.md) for the operating convention.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /home/yu/.claude/plugins/cache/nowledge-community/nowledge-mem/0.7.26/skills/distill-memory

# Distill Memory

Save proactively when the conversation produces a durable fact, preference, decision, plan, procedure, learning, event, or important context. Do not wait to be asked.

## When to Suggest (Moment Detection)

**Breakthrough:** Extended debugging resolves, user relief ("Finally!", "Aha!"), root cause found

**Decision:** Compared options, chose with rationale, trade-off resolved

**Research:** Investigated multiple approaches, conclusion reached, optimal path determined

**Twist:** Unexpected cause-effect, counterintuitive solution, assumption challenged

**Lesson:** "Next time do X", preventive measure, pattern recognized

**Skip:** Routine fixes, work in progress, simple Q&A, generic info

## Memory Quality

**Good (atomic + actionable):**

- "React hooks cleanup must return function. Caused leaks."
- "PostgreSQL over MongoDB: ACID needed for transactions."

**Poor:** Vague "Fixed bugs", conversation transcript

## Tool Usage

Use `nmem` CLI to create memories:

```bash
nmem m add "Insight + context for future use" \
  -t "Searchable title (50-60 chars)" \
  -i 0.8
```

Add `--unit-type fact|preference|decision|plan|procedure|learning|context|event` when the type is clear.

If an existing memory already captures the same decision, workflow, or preference and the new information refines it, update that memory instead of creating a duplicate:

```bash
nmem m update <id> -t "Updated title"
```

**Content:** Outcome/insight focus, include "why", enough context

**Importance:** 0.8-1.0 major | 0.5-0.7 useful | 0.3-0.4 minor

**Note:** For programmatic use, add `--json` flag to get JSON response

**Examples:**

```bash
# High-value insight
nmem m add "React hooks cleanup must return function. Caused memory leaks in event listeners." \
  -t "React Hooks Cleanup Pattern" \
  -i 0.9

# Decision with context
nmem m add "Chose PostgreSQL over MongoDB for ACID compliance and complex queries" \
  -t "Database: PostgreSQL" \
  -i 0.9
```

## Suggestion

**Timing:** After resolution/decision, when user pauses

**Pattern:** "This [type] seems valuable - [essence]. Distill into memory?"

**Frequency:** 1-3 per session typical, quality over quantity

## Troubleshooting

If `nmem` is not in PATH: `pip install nmem-cli`, or on Arch Linux `yay -S nmem-cli` / `paru -S nmem-cli`

For remote servers: run `nmem config client set url https://...` and `nmem config client set api-key ...` once on this machine.

Run `/status` to check server connection.

skills.name: tdd
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /home/yu/.claude/skills/tdd

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.

When exploring the codebase, read the repo's terminology home (a `GLOSSARY.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, or `docs/domain-model.md` — whatever it keeps, if it keeps one) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams: where tests go

A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.

When the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with "codebase-design" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.

## Anti-patterns

- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /home/yu/.claude/skills/codebase-design

# Codebase Design

Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface. Use this language and these principles wherever code is being designed or restructured. The aim is leverage for callers, locality for maintainers, and testability for everyone.

## Glossary

Use these terms exactly: don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary." Consistent language is the whole point.

**Module**: anything with an interface and an implementation. Deliberately scale-agnostic: a function, class, package, or tier-spanning slice. _Avoid_: unit, component, service.

**Interface**: everything a caller must know to use the module correctly: the type signature, but also invariants, ordering constraints, error modes, required configuration, and performance characteristics. _Avoid_: API, signature (too narrow, they refer only to the type-level surface).

**Implementation**: what's inside a module, its body of code. Distinct from **Adapter**: a thing can be a small adapter with a large implementation (a Postgres repo) or a large adapter with a small implementation (an in-memory fake). Reach for "adapter" when the seam is the topic; "implementation" otherwise.

**Depth**: leverage at the interface. The amount of behaviour a caller (or test) can exercise per unit of interface they have to learn. A module is **deep** when a large amount of behaviour sits behind a small interface, **shallow** when the interface is nearly as complex as the implementation.

**Seam** _(Michael Feathers)_: a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place; the *location* at which a module's interface lives. Where to put the seam is its own design decision, distinct from what goes behind it. _Avoid_: boundary (overloaded with DDD's bounded context).

**Adapter**: a concrete thing that satisfies an interface at a seam. Describes *role* (what slot it fills), not substance (what's inside).

**Leverage**: what callers get from depth. More capability per unit of interface they learn. One implementation pays back across N call sites and M tests.

**Locality**: what maintainers get from depth. Change, bugs, knowledge, and verification concentrate in one place rather than spreading across callers. Fix once, fixed everywhere.

## Deep vs shallow

**Deep module** = small interface + lots of implementation:

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│   Small Interface   │  ← Few methods, simple params
├─────────────────────┤
│                     │
│  Deep Implementation│  ← Complex logic hidden
│                     │
└─────────────────────┘
```

**Shallow module** = large interface + little implementation (avoid):

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐

# Skill Manager

A skill preserves a reusable way of working. It is not a memory, a personal preference, or a record of one event.

## Decide

Create or revise a skill when the method has been demonstrated in real work and will make later work clearer or more reliable. Keep one-off work, changing facts, and personal continuity in their ordinary notes.

## Create Or Install

A skill is a directory named `<skill-name>/` containing `SKILL.md`. The location that matters is the directory the current harness discovers skills from; common conventions:

| Harness | Global | Project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pi | `~/.pi/agent/skills/` | `.pi/skills/` (project root) |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/` | `.claude/skills/` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/skills/` | — |

"Install" means creating or copying the directory into the chosen root; no registration command is needed. When unsure where the current harness looks, check its docs before placing files; if the target harness or scope is ambiguous, ask the user. For the Pi harness, install globally under `~/.pi/agent/skills/` unless the user asks for a project-local skill.

When skills are maintained in a source repository, prefer installing by symlink rather than by copy — copies drift stale as the repository evolves:

```bash
ln -s /abs/path/to/repo/skills/<group>/<skill-name> ~/.pi/agent/skills/<skill-name>
```

Harnesses follow the link and read the live files, so one repository update reaches every harness at once. Re-create links only when a skill is added, renamed, or moved.

Keeping several roots in step by hand does not scale; run `scripts/sync_installs.py` (beside this file) to sync them in one pass. It adds links for new skills, relinks moved ones, and removes links to retired ones. It manages only links that resolve into this repository: plain directories and foreign symlinks are reported and left alone, and a same-named stale copy is swapped for the repository link only under `--replace-copies` (`--dry-run` previews every action).

Use a short lowercase hyphenated name. Keep the directory name and the `name` field the same.

```md
---
name: skill-name
description: What this skill does and when to use it.
---
```

Declare the invocation kind in frontmatter: omit `disable-model-invocation` for model-invoked, or set it to `true` for user-invoked (see [Skill Mechanics](references/skill-mechanics.md)).

Read an offered skill before adopting it. Do not write harness-specific install paths into a skill body that must stay portable; state location conventions only when the skill is inherently about installation.

## Write

Describe the method the next Agent needs, not general advice it already knows. Make the description name the real triggers. Keep the main instructions short. Put substantial scripts, references, or templates beside `SKILL.md` only when they are repeatedly useful.

Use clear completion checks for fragile work. For a substantial new or revised skill, read [Writing Great Skills](references/writing-great-skills.md) for the writing methodology (the two loads, pointers, information hierarchy, leading words, pruning) and [Skill Mechanics](references/skill-mechanics.md) for frontmatter, the invocation choice, splitting, and this repository's index rules.

## Review

Read the finished skill once. Check that its name, description, directory, and method agree, and that no existing skill already owns the same method or name.

Writing or changing a skill does not add tools, credentials, permissions, or external services. Harnesses scan skill locations at startup: the current session keeps its existing skill list, and a later session discovers the change.

## Configuration and credentials

A skill that needs an API key, token, or other secret keeps it in its own `auth.json` (JSON, one file per skill) and reads it from there at run time; it does not put the secret in `SKILL.md`, scripts, messages, or other persisted text. Non-secret settings live in `config.json` beside it. Document the exact read/use convention in the skill's `SKILL.md` (file names, expected JSON shape, and how scripts consume them). When installing or creating a skill, follow the same layout and reference it in the skill's `SKILL.md`. See [Configuration and Credentials for Skills](references/auth-and-config.md) for the operating convention.

# Distill Memory

Save proactively when the conversation produces a durable fact, preference, decision, plan, procedure, learning, event, or important context. Do not wait to be asked.

## When to Suggest (Moment Detection)

**Breakthrough:** Extended debugging resolves, user relief ("Finally!", "Aha!"), root cause found

**Decision:** Compared options, chose with rationale, trade-off resolved

**Research:** Investigated multiple approaches, conclusion reached, optimal path determined

**Twist:** Unexpected cause-effect, counterintuitive solution, assumption challenged

**Lesson:** "Next time do X", preventive measure, pattern recognized

**Skip:** Routine fixes, work in progress, simple Q&A, generic info

## Memory Quality

**Good (atomic + actionable):**

- "React hooks cleanup must return function. Caused leaks."
- "PostgreSQL over MongoDB: ACID needed for transactions."

**Poor:** Vague "Fixed bugs", conversation transcript

## Tool Usage

Use `nmem` CLI to create memories:

```bash
nmem m add "Insight + context for future use" \
  -t "Searchable title (50-60 chars)" \
  -i 0.8
```

Add `--unit-type fact|preference|decision|plan|procedure|learning|context|event` when the type is clear.

If an existing memory already captures the same decision, workflow, or preference and the new information refines it, update that memory instead of creating a duplicate:

```bash
nmem m update <id> -t "Updated title"
```

**Content:** Outcome/insight focus, include "why", enough context

**Importance:** 0.8-1.0 major | 0.5-0.7 useful | 0.3-0.4 minor

**Note:** For programmatic use, add `--json` flag to get JSON response

**Examples:**

```bash
# High-value insight
nmem m add "React hooks cleanup must return function. Caused memory leaks in event listeners." \
  -t "React Hooks Cleanup Pattern" \
  -i 0.9

# Decision with context
nmem m add "Chose PostgreSQL over MongoDB for ACID compliance and complex queries" \
  -t "Database: PostgreSQL" \
  -i 0.9
```

## Suggestion

**Timing:** After resolution/decision, when user pauses

**Pattern:** "This [type] seems valuable - [essence]. Distill into memory?"

**Frequency:** 1-3 per session typical, quality over quantity

## Troubleshooting

If `nmem` is not in PATH: `pip install nmem-cli`, or on Arch Linux `yay -S nmem-cli` / `paru -S nmem-cli`

For remote servers: run `nmem config client set url https://...` and `nmem config client set api-key ...` once on this machine.

Run `/status` to check server connection.

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.

When exploring the codebase, read the repo's terminology home (a `GLOSSARY.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, or `docs/domain-model.md` — whatever it keeps, if it keeps one) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams: where tests go

A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.

When the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with "codebase-design" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.

## Anti-patterns

- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.
